title: Kidney cortex: a glomerulus and its tubules
blurb: A thin slice of the outer kidney: one renal corpuscle (a tuft of capillaries inside its capsule), tubules cut across with a fuzzy brush border on the proximal ones, and small capillaries between. Glomerulus size is human; a bird kidney differs. Click a part.
note: Schematic, not a micrograph: shapes are simple solids and the tubules are cut across so that each shows as a ring. Real sizes: the glomerular tuft is drawn 201 micrometres across, the mean of 720 glomeruli in 24 normal adult men, calculated from volume assuming a sphere (Weibel and Gomez method revisited, PMC2375741); the proximal tubule is drawn 44 and the distal tubule 40 micrometres across, the long outer diameters measured in mouse kidney sections (Kidney and Blood Pressure Research 46:229), used here as a stand-in because no dog value was found; tubule diameters differ between species and with how they are measured, and in people the proximal tubule is said to be about 60 micrometres across (a textbook summary, not opened here), so the tubules are drawn narrower than human, and a human distal tubule is clearly narrower than the proximal one, which this pair does not show. The glomerulus size is human only: reported dog renal corpuscles are said to be about half as wide (about 120 micrometres for the whole corpuscle; a thesis seen only in a search snippet and not confirmed here), so this scene is not claimed for the dog. Illustrative sizes: the width of Bowman space (15 micrometres), the capsule, the capillary loops inside the tuft, the two arterioles, the peritubular capillaries (9 micrometres), the clear space inside each tubule, the microvilli of the brush border (drawn 5 micrometres long and 1.2 micrometres thick so that they can be seen; real ones are thought to be shorter, about 1 to 2 micrometres, and far thinner, about 0.1 micrometre, neither measured here), the thickness of the slice (70 micrometres, so the glomerulus is drawn whole and uncut, larger than the thickness of the cut-across tubules), how many tubules are drawn and where they lie. Human sizes for the glomerulus; other mammals share the shape only. Not drawn: the macula densa, the mesangium, the podocytes, the collecting ducts, the connective tissue between the tubules and the junction of the capsule with the tubule (the first tubule section lies against the capsule on the side opposite the vessels, with no opening drawn). Vessels are drawn as straight stubs that stop at the capsule. A bird kidney differs: most of its nephrons are the loopless, reptilian type (about 75-80 percent in domestic fowl) and only a minority have a loop of Henle; this scene has not been drawn for a robin and no robin sizes were found.

labels.text: Afferent (wider) and efferent (narrower) arterioles; drawn stopping at the capsule
